name: Photopea
tagline: Free browser-based image editor that opens Photoshop files, funded by ads
timeToFirstDollar: ~3.5 years (7,000 hours of unpaid work before adding ads)
summary: Photopea is a free web image editor built by Ukrainian-born, Prague-based developer Ivan Kutskir that opens PSD and other formats in the browser. It earns mainly from display ads plus an ad-free Premium subscription and licensing. Kutskir made about $500K in 2020, nearly $1M over the 12 months to April 2021, and told Failory in September 2021 that ads bring in about $100K a month. Latka estimates 2024 revenue at about $2.8M (estimate).
origin: Kutskir had an idea in 2012, while studying computer science in Prague, for a website that displays PSD files, and released the first version (a PSD viewer) in 2013. It gradually became a full editor. By his 2018 Reddit AMA he said he had put about 7,000 hours into it over 3.5 years without earning a dollar before adding ads. He has worked on it full time since finishing his master's degree in 2017.
howItMakesMoney: Display ads to free users (almost 90% of revenue per AIN in 2021; about 6 cents per hour of use per Kutskir), a Premium subscription that removes ads (5 USD/month per the Photopea blog), and licensing deals for companies that embed or self-host Photopea.
growth: Solved a specific need: opening and editing PSD files for free without installing Photoshop
Kutskir posted about it on Reddit, Hacker News and in comments under 'Photoshop alternatives' articles, and asked YouTubers to review it
A Reddit AMA in November 2018 brought a wave of new users
Visitors grew from about 3,000 a month in March 2014, doubling roughly every six months by his account
Very low running costs (about $50 a year for hosting, since everything runs in the browser) let almost all revenue be profit
moat: Years of solo work on file-format compatibility (PSD, XCF, Sketch and more) that is hard to replicate, plus strong search presence as the free Photoshop alternative.
risks: Heavy reliance on ad networks and search traffic; Adobe's own web and free tiers or AI image tools could erode usage.

timeline.event: Starts building a browser PSD viewer
Finishes master's degree and works on Photopea full time; monetization with ads has started
Earns about $20K for the year; Reddit AMA in November brings a wave of new users
Reports nearly $1M over the previous 12 months
Tells Failory ads bring in about $100K/month from 10M monthly visits

lessons: A free tool that replaces an expensive incumbent for a narrow job can grow without marketing spend
Ads work when usage is large and sessions are long
Long pre-revenue periods are survivable when costs are near zero
Doing all the code yourself can make maintenance and fixes faster

rebuild.idea: A free browser tool that opens and edits a proprietary professional file format with no good free viewer, such as CAD/DWG or InDesign packages, monetized by ads and a pro tier
rebuild.why: Browsers (WebAssembly, WebGPU) can now handle heavy files, and many people receive these files occasionally without owning the expensive software.
mvp: Pick one format and build a read-only viewer that opens common files in the browser
Post it in subreddits and forums where people ask how to open that format
Add one basic edit or export feature users request most
Add a single ad slot and a $5/month ad-free option
rebuild.fit: A strong low-level developer comfortable reverse-engineering file formats
rebuild.pricing: Keep the viewer free with one ad slot, and sell a $5/month ad-free plan plus a $20/month pro tier for editing and export features.
rebuild.market: Users are contractors, students and small-office staff who receive DWG or InDesign files occasionally, reached through SEO on 'open DWG online' searches and forum answers. Competitors are Autodesk Viewer, ShareCAD and Adobe's own free viewers.

sources.title: Failory: Building a Photo Editor and Making $100k/mo as a Solo Founder
AIN: Ukrainian single-handedly creates Photopea and makes $1M per year
